newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ retail sales trend rises 0.5 pct Jun qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ retail sales trend rises 0.5 pct Jun qtr.

text.p: The underlying trend in New Zealand retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the June quarter, with a slight decrease in the trend from May to June, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.

After adjusting for seasonal effects and price inflation, retail sales for the June quarter rose two percent over the March quarter. Seasonally adjusted sales at constant prices were NZ$9.65 billion in the June quarter.

Actual retail sales rose 0.2 percent, or NZ$19 million, from the June 1996 quarter, to $9.46 billion in the June 1997 quarter. SNZ said that excluding both motor vehicle storetypes, actual retail sales rose 3.6 percent.
SNZ said the food retailing storetype recorded the largest dollar increase, up $122 million.

Other storetypes to record significant dollar rises in actual retail sales were chemists, up $47 million, and recreational goods outlets, up $26 million. The largest fall was recorded by motor vehicle retailing outlets, down $209 million.

The North and South Islands both recorded rises in retail sales of 0.2 percent between the June 1996 and June 1997 quarters. The Wellington regional council area recorded the largest regional rise, up 4.7 percent.
SNZ said retail stock levels recorded a 5.3 percent decrease from the end of the June 1996 quarter to the end of the June 1997 quarter.
Actual retail sales for the June month were $3.04 billion, a rise of 1.1 percent over June 1996. That followed a May decrease of 3.2 percent.
Actual retail sales rose 0.9 percent in the year ended June 1997 when compared to the June 1996 year.
Seasonally adjusted retail sales rose to $9.7 billion in the June quarter, representing a 1.6 percent rise over the March quarter.
